aliases: Loan terms; Loan characteristics; Syndicate structure; Syndicate concentration; Credit line lending; Term loan lending

name: Bank debt reliance
definition: The extent to which a firm finances itself through relationship-based bank debt rather than arm's-length public debt and equity markets.
sign_convention: higher values mean greater reliance on bank debt relative to arm's-length financing
citations: Rauh, J. D., & Sufi, A. (2010). Capital structure and debt structure. Review of Financial Studies, 23(12), 4242-4280.
aliases: Bank debt share; Bank financing; Private debt share; Debt structure; Arm's length financing (reverse); Multiple bank relationships (reverse)

name: Reference group selection
definition: The choice of the comparison organizations against which a focal organization evaluates its own performance, including how similar the chosen referents are and how often the set is revised.
sign_convention: higher values mean more of the named attribute of the chosen reference group
aliases: Reference group; Comparison group selection; Referent selection; Reference group similarity; Reference group adaptation

name: Value relevance of accounting information
definition: The degree to which investors rely on accounting signals such as earnings or book value when valuing a firm.
sign_convention: higher values mean investors rely more heavily on the accounting signal in valuing the firm
aliases: Value relevance; Reliance on earnings; Reliance on book value; Earnings response

name: Development process concurrency
definition: The degree to which successive stages of a development process, such as design and manufacturing engineering, are carried out simultaneously rather than sequentially.
sign_convention: higher values mean more overlap among development stages
aliases: Process concurrency; Concurrent engineering; Stage overlap; Activity overlapping

name: Ecosystem innovation challenges
definition: The extent to which innovation required in the components supplied upstream or in the complements used downstream must be resolved before a focal technology can create value.
sign_convention: higher values mean greater innovation challenges elsewhere in the ecosystem
citations: Adner, R., & Kapoor, R. (2010). Value creation in innovation ecosystems: how the structure of technological interdependence affects firm performance in new technology generations. Strategic Management Journal, 31(3), 306-333.
aliases: Component innovation challenge; Complement innovation challenge; Ecosystem bottlenecks; Ecosystem emergence challenge

name: Experience pacing
definition: The temporal distribution of an organization's experience, reflected in the length of the intervals between successive occurrences of an activity.
sign_convention: higher values mean longer intervals between successive experience events
aliases: Experience spacing; Interiteration timing; Temporal spacing of experience; Pacing of experience accumulation

name: Feedback delay
definition: The time that elapses between an action and the realization of its outcomes, which shapes how readily actors can learn from feedback.
sign_convention: higher values mean longer delays between actions and their outcomes
aliases: Feedback delays; Outcome delay; Delayed feedback

name: Innovation attributes
definition: Perceived characteristics of an innovation, such as its risk, complexity, skill requirements and observability, that govern how readily it is adopted.
sign_convention: higher values mean more of the named innovation attribute
citations: Rogers, E. M. (2003). Diffusion of Innovations (5th ed.). New York: Free Press.
aliases: Innovation characteristics; Perceived attributes of innovations; Innovation adoptability

name: Innovation barriers
definition: Internal and external obstacles, such as costs and risks, lack of qualified personnel and regulation, that hinder a firm's innovation activities.
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger obstacles to innovation
aliases: Obstacles to innovation; Barriers to innovation; Innovation constraints; Constraints on the application of resources

name: Innovation championing
definition: Advocacy by individuals who actively promote an innovation or project and mobilize support and resources for it within the organization.
sign_convention: higher values mean more or stronger championing of the innovation
citations: Howell, J. M., & Higgins, C. A. (1990). Champions of technological innovation. Administrative Science Quarterly, 35(2), 317-341.
aliases: Champions; Product champion; Project championing; Innovation champion; Dual-role champion; Antagonism (reverse)

name: Invention commercialization
definition: The transformation of an invention into a product or service that is sold on the market.
sign_convention: higher values mean more (or more likely) commercialization
aliases: Technology commercialization; Commercialization of inventions; Commercial use of inventions

name: Knowledge base decomposability
definition: The extent to which a knowledge base can be divided into clusters of tightly coupled knowledge domains that are only loosely coupled with each other.
sign_convention: higher values mean a more decomposable knowledge base
citations: Yayavaram, S., & Ahuja, G. (2008). Decomposability in knowledge structures and its impact on the usefulness of inventions and knowledge-base malleability. Administrative Science Quarterly, 53(2), 333-362.
aliases: Decomposability; Knowledge structure decomposability; Near-decomposability of knowledge

name: Knowledge depreciation
definition: The erosion over time of knowledge acquired through experience, so that past experience contributes less to current knowledge.
sign_convention: higher values mean faster loss of accumulated knowledge
citations: Argote, L., Beckman, S. L., & Epple, D. (1990). The persistence and transfer of learning in industrial settings. Management Science, 36(2), 140-154.
aliases: Organizational forgetting; Forgetting; Knowledge decay; Knowledge retention (reverse)

name: Knowledge protection
definition: Efforts and arrangements through which an organization prevents its proprietary knowledge from being absorbed, imitated or used by others, such as secrecy and restrictive terms of use.
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger protection of proprietary knowledge
aliases: Protection of proprietary assets; Secrecy; Trade secrecy; Knowledge leakage prevention; Knowledge openness (reverse); License openness (reverse); Technology disclosure (reverse)

name: Learning intent
definition: The desire and determination of an organization to acquire knowledge and skills from its partners or external sources.
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger intent to learn
citations: Hamel, G. (1991). Competition for competence and inter-partner learning within international strategic alliances. Strategic Management Journal, 12(S1), 83-103.
aliases: Learning objectives; Intent to learn; Organizational learning intent

name: Market for technology thickness
definition: The intensity of trade in patents and other technology assets in a sector's secondary markets for technology.
sign_convention: higher values mean more active markets for technology
citations: Arora, A., Fosfuri, A., & Gambardella, A. (2001). Markets for Technology: The Economics of Innovation and Corporate Strategy. Cambridge, MA: MIT Press.
aliases: Markets for technology; Patent market liquidity; Technology market activity; Secondary patent market thickness

name: Not-sold-here attitude
definition: Protective attitudes within an organization against exploiting its own knowledge externally, for example through licensing it to other firms.
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger resistance to external knowledge exploitation
aliases: NSH; Not-sold-here syndrome; Not-sold-here tendencies

name: Open source contribution
definition: Contribution of code, review or new projects by organizations or individuals to open source software and similar crowdsourced public goods.
sign_convention: higher values mean more contribution to the open source community
aliases: Contribution to crowdsourced public goods; Open source participation; FOSS contribution; Code contribution; Project launching

name: Organizational memory
definition: Stored knowledge from an organization's history, including declarative knowledge of facts and procedural knowledge of routines, that can be brought to bear on present decisions.
sign_convention: higher values mean more or more accessible organizational memory
citations: Walsh, J. P., & Ungson, G. R. (1991). Organizational memory. Academy of Management Review, 16(1), 57-91.
aliases: Declarative memory; Procedural memory; Organizational memory capacity; Organizational memory level

name: Research appliedness
definition: The degree to which research activity is oriented toward practical application rather than toward basic or fundamental understanding.
sign_convention: higher values mean more applied (less basic) research
aliases: Applied research orientation; Basic research (reverse); Fundamental research (reverse); Appliedness of science

name: Success experience
definition: An organization's or individual's accumulated experience of prior successes in an activity, from which learning can occur.
sign_convention: higher values mean more prior success experience
citations: Madsen, P. M., & Desai, V. (2010). Failing to learn? The effects of failure and success on organizational learning in the global orbital launch vehicle industry. Academy of Management Journal, 53(3), 451-476.
aliases: Prior success; Own success experience; Cumulative wins; Success history

name: Technological complementarity
definition: The degree to which technologies in different layers or components of a system reinforce one another's value when used together.
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger complementarity between technologies
aliases: Complementarity between technologies; Platform layer complementarity; Hardware-software complementarity

name: Top management support for innovation
definition: The degree to which top managers are involved in and encourage product innovation activities in the firm.
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger top management support for innovation
aliases: Management support for innovation; Senior management support; Top management involvement in innovation

name: User innovation
definition: Innovation developed by the users of a product or service, rather than by its producer, to meet their own needs.
sign_convention: higher values mean more (or more likely) user innovation
citations: von Hippel, E. (2005). Democratizing Innovation. Cambridge, MA: MIT Press.
aliases: User-developed innovation; User modifications; Consumer innovation

name: Vacillation
definition: Temporal shifting of an organization's emphasis between exploration and exploitation, as opposed to pursuing both simultaneously.
sign_convention: higher values mean more frequent or larger shifts between exploration and exploitation
citations: Boumgarden, P., Nickerson, J., & Zenger, T. R. (2012). Sailing into the wind: exploring the relationships among ambidexterity, vacillation, and organizational performance. Strategic Management Journal, 33(6), 587-610.
aliases: Vacillation frequency; Vacillation scale; Sequential ambidexterity; Punctuated equilibrium between exploration and exploitation

name: Acquisition capability
definition: A firm's capability to identify, evaluate and integrate acquisition targets.
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger acquisition capability
aliases: M&A capability; Acquisition competence; Acquisition integration capability

name: Environmental capabilities
definition: An organization's capabilities for reducing the environmental harm of its operations, such as preventing pollution and waste.
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger environmental capabilities
citations: Hart, S. L. (1995). A natural-resource-based view of the firm. Academy of Management Review, 20(4), 986-1014.
aliases: Environmental capability; Green capabilities; Pollution prevention capability

name: Inventory investment
definition: The capital a firm has deployed in inventories of materials, work in progress and finished goods.
sign_convention: higher values mean more capital held in inventory
aliases: Inventory level; Inventory holdings; Inventory intensity

name: Political capabilities
definition: A firm's expertise in dealing with and influencing political and regulatory authorities, typically developed through experience in politically challenging environments.
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger political capabilities
citations: Holburn, G. L. F., & Zelner, B. A. (2010). Political capabilities, policy risk, and international investment strategy: evidence from the global electric power generation industry. Strategic Management Journal, 31(12), 1290-1315.
aliases: Political competence; Nonmarket capabilities; Political capability

name: Resource accumulation lag
definition: The time a firm needs to accumulate the resources required to produce output in a product market.
sign_convention: higher values mean longer time needed to build resources
aliases: Time to build; Accumulation lag; Resource build time

name: Relative resource strength
definition: The strength of one organization's resource position compared with that of a counterpart, such as an acquisition target relative to its acquirer.
sign_convention: higher values mean the counterpart holds stronger resources relative to the focal organization
aliases: Resource asymmetry; Relative resource position; Relative resource endowment

name: Resource rarity
definition: The extent to which a resource or capability is possessed by few competing firms.
sign_convention: higher values mean a rarer resource
citations: Barney, J. (1991). Firm resources and sustained competitive advantage. Journal of Management, 17(1), 99-120.
aliases: Rareness; Resource rareness; Capability rarity; Rarity

name: Resource value
definition: The extent to which a resource or capability enables a firm to reduce costs or exploit opportunities and neutralize threats in its environment.
sign_convention: higher values mean a more valuable resource
citations: Barney, J. (1991). Firm resources and sustained competitive advantage. Journal of Management, 17(1), 99-120.
aliases: Resource valuableness; Capability value; Strategic value of resources

name: Expansion rhythm irregularity
definition: The degree to which expansion events such as acquisitions or foreign market entries occur at an uneven rather than a steady, regular pace over time.
sign_convention: higher values mean a more irregular expansion rhythm
citations: Vermeulen, F., & Barkema, H. (2002). Pace, rhythm, and scope: Process dependence in building a profitable multinational corporation. Strategic Management Journal, 23(7).
aliases: Expansion rhythm; Acquisition rhythm; Variability of acquisition rate; Irregularity of expansion; Entry rhythm

name: Financialization
definition: The extent to which a nonfinancial firm allocates its assets and activities to financial investments rather than to its productive operations.
sign_convention: higher values mean a larger share of assets devoted to financial activities
aliases: Financial asset investment; Financial asset share; Corporate financialization

name: Private equity buyout
definition: The acquisition of a firm or business by a private equity investor, typically financed with substantial debt and followed by active ownership, as opposed to acquisition by a corporate buyer.
sign_convention: higher values mean the firm or unit is (more likely) acquired by a private equity firm
aliases: Private equity acquisition; Leveraged buyout; LBO; PE buyout

name: Real options reasoning
definition: The use of real options logic in resource allocation, in which investments are made in small initial steps, kept non-committal and expanded, reallocated or abandoned as uncertainty resolves.
sign_convention: higher values mean more staged, tentative, option-like resource allocation
citations: McGrath, R. G. (1999). Falling forward: Real options reasoning and entrepreneurial failure. Academy of Management Review, 24(1).
aliases: Real options logic; Staged resource allocation; Sequential investment; Tentative commitment; Low initial commitment

name: Customer contact
definition: The degree to which customers are present and interact with the firm's employees during the production and delivery of a service, so that production and consumption occur jointly.
sign_convention: higher values mean more customer contact
aliases: Customer contact intensity; Service inseparability; Inseparability of production and consumption; Buyer-seller interaction intensity

name: Transaction size
definition: The monetary value of individual exchanges between a buyer and a seller, reflecting the financial stakes and purchasing effort attached to each transaction.
sign_convention: higher values mean larger transactions
aliases: Dollar outlay; Order size; Transaction value; Purchase size

name: Activity system interdependence
definition: The extent to which the value of how a firm performs one activity depends on how it performs its other activities, so that activities form a tightly coupled system.
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger interdependence among activities
citations: Rivkin, J. W. (2000). Imitation of complex strategies. Management Science, 46(6).
aliases: Activity interdependence; Interdependency among activities; Complementarity among activities; Fit among activities

name: Brand architecture
definition: The way a firm structures and names its brands, products or units, ranging from extending a common umbrella name across offerings to giving them separate, autonomous brand names.
sign_convention: higher values mean more extension of a common umbrella name across offerings (less naming autonomy)
aliases: Umbrella branding; Branding hierarchy; Family branding; Branded house versus house of brands; Name seeding

name: Efficiency-centered business model design
definition: The extent to which a firm's business model is designed to reduce transaction costs and increase transaction efficiency for all participants in its activity system.
sign_convention: higher values mean a more efficiency-centered business model design
citations: Zott, C., & Amit, R. (2007). Business model design and the performance of entrepreneurial firms. Organization Science, 18(2).
aliases: Business model efficiency; Efficiency-centered business model; Efficiency business model design theme

name: Openness strategy
definition: The extent to which a firm grants outsiders access to, or control over, its technologies, products or platform through open standards, open-source offerings, licensing or shared governance, rather than keeping them proprietary and closed.
sign_convention: higher values mean a more open (less proprietary or restrictive) strategy
citations: Boudreau, K. (2010). Open platform strategies and innovation: Granting access vs. devolving control. Management Science, 56(10).
aliases: Platform openness; Open versus proprietary strategy; Business model openness; Open technology strategy; Standards-based strategy; Platform access policy

name: Competitive action unpredictability
definition: The extent to which the sequence and pattern of a firm's competitive actions varies from one period or attack to the next, making its behavior hard for rivals to anticipate.
sign_convention: higher values mean less predictable competitive actions
aliases: Attack unpredictability; Competitive unpredictability; Action sequence variability

name: Competitive repertoire similarity
definition: The extent to which two rival firms deploy similar sets and mixes of competitive action types.
sign_convention: higher values mean more similar action repertoires
aliases: Competitive similarity; Action repertoire similarity; Competitive dissimilarity (reverse)

name: Competitor identification mismatch
definition: The discrepancy between whether a firm treats another firm as a comparable competitor and whether customers treat the two firms as comparable alternatives.
sign_convention: higher values mean a larger mismatch between firm and customer competitor definitions
aliases: Competitor comparison mismatch; Self-asserted comparison; Self-dismissed comparison; Competitor definition misalignment

name: Customer co-production
definition: The degree to which customers actively participate in the design and delivery of the firm's product or service offering.
sign_convention: higher values mean more customer participation in production
aliases: Co-production; Customer participation; Value co-creation with customers

name: Customer financial value
definition: The revenue or profit a customer or customer segment generates for the firm, which distinguishes more from less lucrative customers.
sign_convention: higher values mean a more financially valuable customer
aliases: Customer profitability; Customer value to the firm; High-paying customer status

name: Distribution intensity
definition: The breadth of a product's or firm's distribution coverage, reflected in the number of outlets, distributors or screens through which it is made available in a market.
sign_convention: higher values mean more intensive (broader, less selective) distribution
aliases: Distribution coverage; Distribution breadth; Retail availability; Distribution selectivity (reverse); Release breadth

name: Economic rent
definition: The surplus that an asset, contract or position yields in excess of its opportunity cost, which the party controlling it can capture.
sign_convention: higher values mean larger rents
aliases: Rents; Contract rent; Surplus value

name: First-mover advantage
definition: The extent to which early entrants into a market can obtain durable advantages over later entrants, for example through technological leadership, preemption of scarce assets or buyer switching costs.
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger first-mover advantages
citations: Lieberman, M. B., & Montgomery, D. B. (1988). First-mover advantages. Strategic Management Journal, 9(S1).
aliases: First mover advantages; Early mover advantages; Pioneering advantage; Preemption opportunity

name: Strategic emphasis
definition: The relative priority and resources a firm gives to different functional activities, in particular value creation activities such as R&D relative to value appropriation activities such as marketing.
sign_convention: no single direction across functional activities; a ratio such as R&D to marketing keeps its numerator and denominator in its measure
citations: Mizik, N., & Jacobson, R. (2003). Trading off between value creation and value appropriation: The financial implications of shifts in strategic emphasis. Journal of Marketing, 67(1).
aliases: Functional emphasis; Functional importance mix; R&D versus marketing emphasis

name: Market entry motives
definition: The reasons for which a firm enters a new market, such as pursuing the market's growth, exploiting existing advantages or defending a position in an existing market.
sign_convention: higher values mean greater importance of the named entry motive
aliases: Entry motives; Entry motivation; Diversification motives; Offensive versus defensive entry

name: Network effects
definition: The extent to which the value a product or platform creates for a user depends on the number of other users, either on the same side (direct) or on another side of a multisided market (indirect or cross-side).
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger network effects
citations: Katz, M. L., & Shapiro, C. (1985). Network externalities, competition, and compatibility. American Economic Review, 75(3).
aliases: Network externalities; Direct network effects; Indirect network effects; Cross-side network effects; Two-sided market externalities; Social product features

name: Output quantity
definition: The quantity of goods or services a firm produces or makes available in a market during a period.
sign_convention: higher values mean greater output
aliases: Production volume; Quantity supplied; Output level; Production quantity

name: Platform complementor base
definition: The size of the complementor side of a platform, reflecting how many complementors or complementary products are available on it.
sign_convention: higher values mean a larger complementor base
aliases: Number of complementors; Complement availability; Complementor ecosystem size; Number of complements

name: Product scarcity
definition: The extent to which the available supply of a product falls short of demand, whether deliberately engineered by the firm or not.
sign_convention: higher values mean greater scarcity
aliases: Scarcity strategy; Limited edition; Supply restriction; Introductory scarcity

name: Strategic commitment
definition: The degree to which a firm's strategic actions are irreversible or signal that the firm will persist with them, binding its future choices.
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger commitment
citations: Ghemawat, P. (1991). Commitment: The Dynamic of Strategy. New York: Free Press.
aliases: Commitment; Entrant commitment; Irreversibility of strategic action; Signaled commitment

name: Value appropriation
definition: The share of the value created by an activity, resource or relationship that a focal actor captures for itself rather than other parties.
sign_convention: higher values mean a larger share of value captured
citations: Lepak, D. P., Smith, K. G., & Taylor, M. S. (2007). Value creation and value capture: A multilevel perspective. Academy of Management Review, 32(1).
aliases: Value capture; Appropriability; Share of value created; Rent appropriation

name: Aggregate FDI flows
definition: The volume of foreign direct investment flowing into a country, or between a pair of countries, in a period, and its change over time.
sign_convention: higher values mean larger FDI inflows
aliases: FDI inflows; Bilateral FDI flows; Inward foreign direct investment; Country-level FDI

name: Bilateral trade dependence
definition: The extent to which a country's economy depends on trade with another specific country.
sign_convention: higher values mean greater economic dependence on the partner country
aliases: Bilateral economic dependence; Trade dependence; Bilateral trade intensity

name: Country-specific advantages
definition: Advantages that firms derive from the resources, institutions and market conditions of their home country, available to firms of that nationality rather than being firm-specific.
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger country-specific advantages
aliases: CSAs; Home-based advantages; Home country advantages; National advantage

name: Cultural attractiveness
definition: The desirability of one country's culture to members of another culture, based on how far the former's practices reflect the latter's values.
sign_convention: higher values mean the target culture is more attractive to the observing culture
aliases: Cultural desirability; Cross-cultural attractiveness

name: Cultural diversity of international operations
definition: The degree to which the cultural characteristics of the countries in which a firm operates differ from one another.
sign_convention: higher values mean more culturally diverse foreign operations
aliases: Cultural variance; Cultural diversity of markets; Cultural heterogeneity of the international portfolio

name: Expatriate staffing
definition: The extent to which a multinational staffs its foreign subsidiaries with expatriates from the parent country, as a means of coordination, control and knowledge transfer.
sign_convention: higher values mean a larger share of expatriate parent-country nationals
aliases: Expatriate assignment; Expatriate ratio; Parent-country national staffing; Expatriate proportion

name: Country globalization
definition: The extent of a country's economic, social and political integration with other countries, which exposes its population and organizations to foreign ideas and norms.
sign_convention: higher values mean a more globalized country
aliases: National globalization; Exposure to global norms; KOF globalization

name: Offshoring
definition: The relocation or sourcing of business functions or services from locations outside the firm's home country, whether performed by the firm's own units or by foreign suppliers.
sign_convention: higher values mean more offshoring
aliases: Offshore outsourcing; Foreign sourcing; International sourcing; Global sourcing

name: Pressure for local responsiveness
definition: The extent to which differences across a multinational's host environments, such as customer needs, market structures and government demands, push it to adapt its activities to each local context.
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger pressure for local responsiveness
citations: Prahalad, C. K., & Doz, Y. L. (1987). The Multinational Mission: Balancing Local Demands and Global Vision. New York: Free Press.
aliases: Local responsiveness pressure; Local responsiveness; Pressures for local adaptation

name: Appropriability regime
definition: The environmental conditions in an industry that govern how well innovators can capture the returns to their innovations, including the effectiveness of patents, secrecy, licensing and control of complementary assets.
sign_convention: higher values mean a stronger appropriability regime (innovators capture more of the returns)
citations: Teece, D. J. 1986. Profiting from technological innovation: Implications for integration, collaboration, licensing and public policy. Research Policy 15(6): 285-305.
aliases: Appropriability conditions; Appropriability mechanisms; Importance of secrecy; Licensing feasibility; Commercialization environment

name: Dominant design
definition: The emergence of a single product design or architecture that wins allegiance in a product class and becomes the standard to which competitors must adhere, marking the shift from an era of ferment to incremental change.
sign_convention: higher values mean a dominant design has emerged or is more firmly established
citations: Anderson, P., & Tushman, M. L. 1990. Technological discontinuities and dominant designs: A cyclical model of technological change. Administrative Science Quarterly 35(4): 604-633.
aliases: Emergence of a dominant design; Industry standard design

name: Dysfunctional competition
definition: The extent to which competition in a firm's environment is opportunistic, unfair or unlawful, as when rivals imitate illegally, violate contracts or exploit weak enforcement.
sign_convention: higher values mean more dysfunctional competition
citations: Li, H., & Atuahene-Gima, K. 2001. Product innovation strategy and the performance of new technology ventures in China. Academy of Management Journal 44(6): 1123-1134.
aliases: Unfair competition; Illegitimate competition; Opportunistic competition

name: Income inequality
definition: The degree to which income is unequally distributed among the members of a society or region.
sign_convention: higher values mean more unequal income distribution
aliases: Gini coefficient; Income dispersion; Economic inequality

name: Industry pollution intensity
definition: The extent to which the activities of an industry generate pollution or emissions relative to its size, reflecting how environmentally harmful the sector is.
sign_convention: higher values mean a more polluting industry
aliases: Sector emissions intensity; Dirty industry; Environmentally sensitive industry

name: Market information environment
definition: The quantity and quality of information about firms, assets or opportunities that is available to market participants, including the extent to which it is hard and verifiable rather than soft.
sign_convention: higher values mean richer, harder and more verifiable information
aliases: Information environment; Information ecosystem; Market transparency

name: Labor migration
definition: The movement of workers between regions or countries, including emigration from and return migration to their places of origin.
sign_convention: higher values mean more migration flows
aliases: Migration; Return migration; Return mobility; Migrant flows

name: Markets for technology
definition: The extent to which technology can be bought, sold or licensed in arm's-length markets, so that firms can obtain the technology they need from external suppliers.
sign_convention: higher values mean more developed markets for technology (easier external technology supply)
citations: Arora, A., Fosfuri, A., & Gambardella, A. 2001. Markets for Technology: The Economics of Innovation and Corporate Strategy. Cambridge, MA: MIT Press.

name: Motherhood wage penalty

name: Country effect

name: Bilateral political volatility

name: Political decentralization

sign_convention: higher values mean more decentralized political authority

name: Board chair resource orientation

name: Strategic decision effectiveness
definition: The extent to which a strategic decision achieves the objectives that management set for it.
sign_convention: higher values mean more effective strategic decisions

name: Executive severance protection

name: National innovative capacity
definition: A country's ability to produce and commercialize a flow of new-to-the-world technologies over the long term, reflecting its common innovation infrastructure and cluster conditions.

aliases: Technology leader country; National innovation capacity; Country innovative productivity

name: Trait-based imitation

citations: Haunschild, P. R., & Miner, A. S. (1997). Modes of interorganizational imitation: The effects of outcome salience and uncertainty. Administrative Science Quarterly, 42(3), 472-500.

name: Labor-management conflict
definition: The level of open conflict between management and the workforce or its representatives, expressed in grievances, disputes and strikes.
sign_convention: higher values mean more labor-management conflict

name: Executive Machiavellianism
definition: The extent to which an executive shows the Machiavellian personality trait: cynical mistrust of others, willingness to manipulate and deceive, and a pragmatic, opportunistic pursuit of self-interest.
sign_convention: higher values mean more Machiavellian
citations: Christie, R., & Geis, F. L. (1970). Studies in Machiavellianism. New York: Academic Press.
aliases: CEO Machiavellianism; Machiavellianism

name: Workplace unionization
definition: The extent to which an organization's or establishment's employees are represented by labor unions or covered by collective agreements, giving them collective bargaining power.
sign_convention: higher values mean more unionized workforce
aliases: Firm unionization; Union status; Union coverage; Employee bargaining power; Unionized workforce

name: Exchange rate
definition: The relative price of a home currency in terms of foreign currencies, in nominal or real terms, which shapes the cost competitiveness of a firm's exports and foreign operations.
sign_convention: higher values mean a weaker (more depreciated) home currency

name: Employee board representation
definition: The presence of directors appointed by or representing employees, often through trade unions under codetermination rules, on a firm's board.
sign_convention: higher values mean more employee representation on the board

name: Quality assurance investment
definition: Expenditures a firm makes to prevent and detect quality problems, including prevention costs that keep defects from being produced and appraisal costs of inspection and testing.
sign_convention: higher values mean more investment in quality assurance
aliases: Prevention costs; Appraisal costs; Cost of quality; Conformance investment; Quality investment

name: Agentic orientation
definition: An individual's motivational emphasis on independence, self-assertion, control over the environment and the pursuit of personal goals.
sign_convention: higher values mean a stronger agentic orientation
aliases: Agency; Agentic values; Agentic motives; Agentic value display

name: Climate strength
definition: The degree of agreement among members of a unit in their perceptions of its climate or of the practices they experience.
sign_convention: higher values mean more consensus (less dispersion) in climate perceptions
aliases: Climate consensus; Homogeneity of HR practice experiences; HR system consensus

name: Financial inclusion
definition: The extent to which individuals and households have access to and use credit and other services from formal financial institutions.
sign_convention: higher values mean more access to formal financial services
aliases: Access to formal credit; Access to formal financial services; Formal borrowing

name: Professional community participation
definition: An individual's in-person involvement in the meetings, conferences and other events of a professional, scientific or technical community.
sign_convention: higher values mean more participation

name: Executive military experience
definition: Prior service of an executive in the armed forces.
sign_convention: higher values mean more (or any) military service
aliases: Military service; Military background; CEO military experience

name: Business group position
definition: The location of a firm within the ownership hierarchy of its business group, from the apex firm that controls the group to affiliates lower in the chain of ownership.
sign_convention: higher values mean a position closer to the apex of the group
aliases: Apex firm; Position in the pyramid; Pyramidal layer

name: Armed conflict exposure
definition: The extent to which an organization or unit is proximally exposed to war or other armed conflict in its operating locations.
sign_convention: higher values mean more exposure to armed conflict

name: Personal responsibility for a decision
definition: The degree to which a decision maker personally made, and is responsible for, an earlier choice that is being evaluated.
sign_convention: higher values mean more personal responsibility

aliases: Personal responsibility; Decision responsibility

name: Job rotation
definition: The systematic movement of employees across jobs, teams or units, so that they spend part of their time outside their home assignment.
sign_convention: higher values mean more rotation
aliases: Team rotation; Rotation; Cross-assignment

name: Management fashion
definition: The transitory collective belief, disseminated by fashion setters such as media and consultants, that a management technique or business idea is at the forefront of rational progress, rising in a boom and fading in a bust.
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger fashion (more positive attention) around the practice or idea
citations: Abrahamson, E. (1996). Management fashion. Academy of Management Review, 21(1), 254-285.
aliases: Fads and fashions; Management fad; Fashion cycle; Fashion boom

name: Technological performance
definition: The performance a technology achieves on the key technical attributes by which it is judged, and its theoretical ceiling given its fundamental principles.
sign_convention: higher values mean better technical performance
aliases: Core technical performance; Technology performance; Technical performance

name: Competitive parity
definition: The extent to which competitors are evenly matched in their past contests or competitive strength.
sign_convention: higher values mean more evenly matched competitors
aliases: Competitiveness of the match-up; Historic competitiveness; Competitive balance

name: Administrative innovation
definition: Innovation in organizational structure, administrative processes and human resource management, which relates to the management of the organization rather than its basic work activity.
sign_convention: higher values mean more administrative innovation
citations: Damanpour, F. (1991). Organizational innovation: A meta-analysis of effects of determinants and moderators. Academy of Management Journal, 34(3), 555-590.
aliases: Management innovation; Organizational innovation (administrative); Nontechnical innovation

name: Network activation
definition: The selection and mobilization of particular contacts from an actor's network for a specific purpose, such as seeking resources or access to a target.
sign_convention: higher values mean more activation of the named contacts
aliases: Social capital mobilization; Contact selection; Cognitive network activation

name: Employer pay premium
definition: The portion of an individual's pay attributable to the organization that employs them rather than to the individual's own characteristics.
sign_convention: higher values mean a larger organization-specific pay premium
aliases: Organizational effect on pay; Firm wage premium; Employer effect

name: CEO prestige power
definition: CEO power derived from the CEO's reputation, standing and elite connections in the firm's institutional environment.
sign_convention: higher values mean more prestige power
citations: Finkelstein, S. (1992). Power in top management teams: Dimensions, measurement, and validation. Academy of Management Journal, 35(3), 505-538.
aliases: Prestige power; Executive prestige power

name: Investor exit pressure
definition: The pressure investors face to liquidate their stakes in a portfolio company, arising for example from the approaching termination of their funds.
sign_convention: higher values mean more pressure to exit
aliases: VC exit pressure; Fund age pressure; Investor impatience

name: Component bottleneck
definition: Whether a component of a multicomponent product system is the constraint that most limits improvement of overall system performance at a given time.
sign_convention: higher values mean the component is (more of) a binding constraint
aliases: Constraint component; Performance bottleneck; Slack component (reverse)

name: Evoked mental imagery
definition: The mental images that a communication, such as a speaker's words or gestures, evokes in the audience, leading them to simulate what is described.
sign_convention: higher values mean more vivid evoked imagery
aliases: Mental imagery; Communication-evoked imagery

name: Secondary share sales at IPO
definition: The sale at the initial public offering of existing shares by pre-IPO owners, such as founders and venture capitalists, as opposed to new primary shares issued by the firm.
sign_convention: higher values mean more selling of secondary shares by pre-IPO owners
aliases: Secondary shares; Founder selling at IPO; VC selling at IPO; Insider cash-out at IPO

name: Prior adoptions of competing innovations
definition: The number of organizations in a focal organization's reference group that have already adopted a rival or substitute innovation instead of the focal one.

name: Population mass
definition: The combined size of the organizations in a population or local market, weighting each organization by its size rather than counting it once as density does.

name: Product density
definition: The number of products of a given kind offered in a market, capturing crowding and legitimation at the level of products rather than organizations.

name: Exchange performance
definition: The degree to which a transaction or supply relationship, whether governed by market, hybrid or hierarchy, meets the buyer's objectives for cost, quality and responsiveness.

name: Rival experience
definition: The accumulated operating experience of the competitors a focal organization faces in its market.

name: Partner industry specialization
definition: The degree to which an organization's exchange partner or intermediary concentrates its activities in the focal organization's industry.

name: Serial temporary advantage
definition: A pattern in which a firm repeatedly regains superior performance after lapses, sustaining advantage through a sequence of temporary advantages rather than one persistent advantage.

name: Top management team distinctiveness
definition: The extent to which the composition of a firm's top management team differs from the typical team composition among its competitive peers.

name: Organizational identity similarity
definition: The degree to which two organizations share the same type of organizational identity, that is, similar answers to the question of what kind of organization each is.

name: Collective decision making
definition: Whether a decision is made by an individual acting alone or by several organization members whose judgments are combined through a decision structure.

name: Government-affiliated intermediary choice
definition: A firm's reliance on government-affiliated rather than private third-party intermediaries to audit, certify or support its compliance with regulation.

name: Primogeniture succession
definition: Whether leadership of a family firm passes to the firstborn child of the departing leader rather than to a later-born offspring.

name: Coworker co-founding
definition: Whether a new venture is founded jointly by individuals who previously worked together in the same parent organization rather than by a founder alone or with outsiders.

name: Innovative cognitive style
definition: An individual's preference for solving problems by doing things differently and departing from existing paradigms rather than by doing things better within them, the innovator pole of the adaptor-innovator continuum.

name: Power values
definition: The importance an individual attaches to social status, prestige and control or dominance over people and resources.

name: Self-direction values
definition: The importance an individual attaches to independent thought and action, including choosing, creating and exploring.

name: Home-base knowledge sourcing
definition: The extent to which a foreign subsidiary's innovation draws on knowledge originating in the parent firm's home country rather than in the host or third countries.

name: Category investment salience
definition: The prominence of recent, widely noticed investment successes in a market category, which signals audience consensus about the category's quality.

name: Identity congruence of claimed elements
definition: The degree to which an issue or attribute an organization takes up is compatible with its own identity rather than tied to the identity of an opposing rival.

name: Strategic heterogeneity
definition: The degree to which the strategies pursued by firms within an industry differ from one another.

name: Performance bright spot
definition: The best performing segment or subunit within a firm's portfolio, whose success can shape how managers interpret and respond to overall performance feedback.
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger performance of the firm's best performing segment
aliases: Bright spot; Product bright spot; Geographic bright spot; Best performing segment

name: Operational performance variability
definition: The variability over time of a unit's operational outputs, such as production volume or quality, reflecting the predictability of its operations.
sign_convention: higher values mean more variable, less predictable operational output
aliases: Production variance; Quality variance; Output predictability (reverse); Operational variability

name: Information access speed
definition: The speed with which decision makers can observe and use information once it becomes available, independent of the content of the information set.
sign_convention: higher values mean shorter delay between information availability and access
aliases: Speed of information access; Data velocity; Information latency (reverse)

name: Enabling technology
definition: The degree to which a technology is pervasive across fields, novel and improvable, and able to spawn complementary innovations.
sign_convention: higher values mean greater enabling potential of the technology
aliases: Enabling technologies; Enabling potential; General purpose technology potential

name: Experience recency
definition: How recently an actor's relevant experience or learning was accumulated, reflecting the currency of the knowledge it holds.
sign_convention: higher values mean more recently acquired experience
aliases: Recency of experience; Recent experience; Experience currency

name: User feedback representativeness

sign_convention: higher values mean feedback providers more closely match the customer base
aliases: Feedback community representativeness; Community unrepresentativeness (reverse); Feedback self-selection (reverse)

name: Functional depth

sign_convention: higher values mean deeper experience in one functional domain

name: T-shaped skills

sign_convention: higher values mean a stronger combination of depth and breadth of experience
aliases: T-shaped experience; T-shaped profile

name: Opportunity cost of resources
definition: The value forgone by keeping resources in their current use rather than redeploying them to their best alternative use within or outside the firm.

name: Termination capability

sign_convention: higher values mean stronger capability to terminate failing investments

name: Stigma distancing

name: Product name emotional valence

name: Product age

sign_convention: higher values mean an older product

name: Competitor ability

sign_convention: higher values mean more able competitors

name: Product cannibalization

sign_convention: higher values mean more demand lost to the organization's own products

name: Service intensity

name: Workplace isolation

sign_convention: higher values mean more isolation from others in the organization

name: Openness to interorganizational cooperation

sign_convention: higher values mean greater openness to interorganizational cooperation

name: Stakeholder governance

name: Managerial foresight

sign_convention: higher values mean more accurate anticipation of future developments

name: Initiating structure

sign_convention: higher values mean more initiating structure behavior

name: Expert power

sign_convention: higher values mean more influence based on expertise

name: Informal control

sign_convention: higher values mean more extensive use of informal control

name: Coordination costs

sign_convention: higher values mean higher coordination costs

name: Unit hierarchical level

name: Market discourse leadership
definition: The extent to which an actor's public discourse leads rather than follows the prevailing discourse in its market, introducing themes that others later adopt.

name: Universalistic allocation criteria

sign_convention: higher values mean greater reliance on universalistic criteria in resource allocation

name: Decision speed
definition: The speed with which an individual or organizational decision maker reaches a decision once a decision problem arises.
sign_convention: higher values mean faster decisions

name: Identity-extending actions

name: Organizational goal stability

sign_convention: higher values mean more stable organizational goals

name: Organizational goal clarity
definition: The extent to which an organization's objectives and policies are specific and clearly stated rather than general and vague.
sign_convention: higher values mean clearer, more specific organizational goals

name: Subjective probability of success

name: Political culture
definition: The shared orientations toward government and politics that characterize the population of a region or country.
sign_convention: higher values mean more of the named political culture type

name: Forces for change

name: Organizational lag

name: Change agent origin

name: Acquisition-based hiring

name: Perceived deservingness

name: Subjective value of money

name: Executive greed

name: Executive psychopathy

sign_convention: higher values mean more psychopathic tendencies

name: Member participation

sign_convention: higher values mean more member participation

name: Challenging nonwork activity
definition: The extent to which an individual's activities outside work are skilled, active and challenging rather than passive.
sign_convention: higher values mean more challenging and creative nonwork activities

name: Venture gestation activity

sign_convention: higher values mean more or longer pre-operational organizing activity

name: Correlated information among market participants

sign_convention: higher values mean more correlated information and judgments

name: Market pricing accuracy

aliases: Valuation accuracy; Pricing accuracy; Price bubbles (reverse); Mispricing (reverse)

name: Urban dominance
definition: The extent to which a city concentrates economic, cultural and organizational activity that serves a wider territory, whether its surrounding region or the nation.
sign_convention: higher values mean greater dominance of the city over the named territory

name: Intermediary dispensability
definition: The extent to which buyers and sellers can transact directly without the services of an intermediary.
sign_convention: higher values mean the intermediary is more easily bypassed
aliases: Disintermediation threat; Intermediary indispensability (reverse)

name: Factor substitutability
definition: The ease with which production inputs such as capital and labor can be substituted for one another in an industry's technology.
sign_convention: higher values mean greater substitutability between factors

name: Legal specificity
definition: The extent to which laws specify what actors must do in terms of procedures, timelines, formulas and contingencies.
sign_convention: higher values mean more specific laws

name: Institutional logic contrast
definition: The extent to which audiences perceive organizations in a field as either clearly associated with or clearly dissociated from an institutional logic.
sign_convention: higher values mean sharper contrast of the logic
aliases: Logic contrast

name: Discriminatory tastes
definition: An actor's preference against transacting with members of a particular group, independent of productivity or profit considerations.
sign_convention: higher values mean stronger discriminatory preferences

aliases: Taste-based discrimination; Discriminatory owner tastes; Prejudice

name: Discriminatory treatment of customers

name: Pollution outsourcing

sign_convention: higher values mean more pollution shifted to suppliers

name: Issue materiality

sign_convention: higher values mean more (or more financially significant) material social and environmental issues
citations: Khan, M., Serafeim, G., & Yoon, A. (2016). Corporate sustainability: First evidence on materiality. The Accounting Review, 91(6), 1697-1724.

aliases: Pipeline orientation

name: Role distribution across units
definition: The extent to which employees holding a given role are spread across different organizational units.
sign_convention: higher values mean the role is spread more evenly across units
aliases: Organizational distribution of a role

name: Job recruiting breadth
definition: The diversity of the roles from which people entering a job are drawn.
sign_convention: higher values mean entrants come from a more diverse set of source roles
aliases: Source role diversity

name: Career atypicality
definition: The degree to which an individual's career sequence departs from the prototypical career paths in an organization.
sign_convention: higher values mean a more atypical career path
aliases: Career departure from prototypical paths

name: Civic action effectiveness
definition: How effective local community action is in raising awareness, funds and other resources for a cause.
sign_convention: higher values mean more effective local civic action
aliases: Effectiveness of local civic action

name: Relational style consistency
definition: The degree to which an actor uses a coherent relational style, or successive actors in a role use the same style.
sign_convention: higher values mean more consistent relational styles
aliases: Individual style consistency; Style continuity across successive actors

name: Innovation quality dispersion
definition: The spread of the quality or impact of a firm's innovations, such as the dispersion of citations received by its patents.
sign_convention: higher values mean a wider dispersion of innovation quality
aliases: Patent quality distribution; Citation dispersion

name: Deadline penalty
definition: A penalty an agent faces at a periodic checkpoint for having incomplete tasks, imposed directly by a principal or indirectly through peers.
sign_convention: higher values mean a heavier penalty for missing deadlines
aliases: Deadline pressure penalty

name: Deadline clustering of activity
definition: The concentration of task completions or transactions at the end of a period or deadline.
sign_convention: higher values mean more activity clustered at period-end deadlines
aliases: Task completion clustering; Period-end sales timing; Month-end origination

name: Online content volume
definition: The amount of content, such as text and images, available on an online page or platform.
sign_convention: higher values mean more online content
aliases: Wikipedia page content; Page content volume

name: Venture capital availability
definition: The amount of venture capital funding available in a region or market for new ventures.
sign_convention: higher values mean more venture capital is available
aliases: Regional venture capital supply

name: Tryout hiring
definition: A hiring practice in which decision makers observe candidates in the actual work setting before making a long-term hiring decision.
sign_convention: higher values mean more hiring through tryouts
aliases: Tryout; Trial employment

name: Contract renegotiation
definition: The revision of the terms of a formal contract after it has been agreed, including ex post adjustments of payment.
sign_convention: higher values mean more renegotiation of the contract
aliases: Ex post renegotiation

name: Audience gender composition
definition: The gender composition of the people who use or engage with a platform or product.
sign_convention: higher values mean a more female audience
aliases: Female user engagement; Female engagement

name: Cognition observability
definition: The extent to which the cognition of others, such as their mental associations, can be inferred from observable cues.
sign_convention: higher values mean another actors cognition is more observable
aliases: Observability of latent cognition

name: Individual risk taking
definition: The extent to which an individual takes actions with uncertain and potentially costly outcomes, observed as behavior rather than as a disposition. Higher values indicate more risk-taking behavior.
sign_convention: higher values mean more risk-taking behavior
aliases: Risk taking behavior; Risky conduct

name: Rank instability
definition: The extent to which competitors change rank positions over a period.
sign_convention: higher values mean more rank changes among competitors
aliases: Rank change; Rank turbulence

name: Media presence
definition: The amount of media outlets, such as magazines, available in a locality, serving as channels for communicating and theorizing ideas.
sign_convention: higher values mean more media presence
aliases: Print media; Specialized media presence

name: Qualified audit opinion
definition: An auditor's opinion that qualifies, rather than fully endorses, a firm's financial statements.
sign_convention: higher values mean the firm received a qualified audit opinion
aliases: Audit qualification; Modified audit opinion

name: Perceived-assessed performance discrepancy
definition: The gap between how an employee perceives his or her own performance and the performance assessed for the employee.
sign_convention: higher values mean a larger gap between perceived and assessed performance
aliases: Self-other performance discrepancy

name: Independent contracting
definition: Whether a worker provides services directly to a client firm on a short-term basis without entering a formal employment relationship.
sign_convention: higher values mean more independent contracting
aliases: Contracting; Freelancing; Contract work

name: Contingent work spell duration
definition: The length of a continuous period of contingent or contract work.
sign_convention: higher values mean longer contingent work spells
aliases: Contracting duration; Long-term contracting

name: Opportunity and resource provision
definition: The resources or opportunities, such as work assignments, that input providers give to a focal actor.
sign_convention: higher values mean more resources or opportunities provided to the actor
aliases: Inputs received; Opportunity provision

name: Knowledge expropriation risk
definition: The risk that a firm's knowledge outflows are obtained and exploited by competitors to the firm's disadvantage.
sign_convention: higher values mean greater risk of knowledge expropriation
aliases: Appropriation risk of knowledge outflows

name: Prospective option wealth
definition: The potential future gain in an executive's option wealth, over and above the value already accumulated in the options, that would be realized if the firm's stock price rises before the options expire. It is distinct from current option wealth, the value already accumulated.
sign_convention: higher values mean a larger potential future gain from the options
aliases: Prospective wealth; CEO prospective option wealth

name: Executive generational cohort
definition: The cohort of executives who completed their education or entered their careers in the same institutional period, such as before or after an economic reform or a change in university admissions. It is not ordinary age.
sign_convention: higher values mean membership in the later cohort
aliases: CEO generational cohort; Post-reform generation

name: Option contract terms
definition: The contractual parameters of an option, such as its exercise (strike) price and its time to expiration. They shape the option value but are not the value itself.
sign_convention: higher values mean a larger parameter value (a higher exercise price, a longer time to expiration)
aliases: Exercise price; Option duration; Time to expiration

name: Audience turnover
definition: The degree to which the members of an actor's audience leave and are replaced over time, so that the audience is unstable. It is distinct from how favorably the audience evaluates the actor.
sign_convention: higher values mean more turnover (a less stable audience)
aliases: Audience instability

name: Insider purchases
definition: Open-market purchases of a firm's shares by its officers, directors and other insiders.
sign_convention: higher values mean more insider buying
aliases: Insider buying

name: Insider sales
definition: Open-market sales of a firm's shares by its officers, directors and other insiders.
sign_convention: higher values mean more insider selling (sales are not negative purchases)
aliases: Insider selling

name: Hiring rate
definition: The number or rate of new employees an organization brings in from outside over a period.
sign_convention: higher values mean more external hires, in number or relative to the workforce
aliases: Number of hires; Hiring volume
